evals.prompt: Trivy keeps flagging Alpine packages in both of our images and I'd like to get rid of most of them by moving the runtime images to Google's distroless Node image. The Dockerfile as it is on main is provided at `.claude/skills/container-hardening/evals/files/Dockerfile.txt` and the compose file at `.claude/skills/container-hardening/evals/files/docker-compose.yml.txt`; treat them as the repo's `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml`. Rewrite them for distroless and tell me what I need to check before I merge.
evals.expected_output: Moves every stage that runs npm ci to a glibc Debian base matching the distroless release (e.g. node:24-bookworm-slim with gcr.io/distroless/nodejs24-debian12) because @node-rs/argon2 and @next/swc install libc-specific prebuilds; turns both HEALTHCHECKs into exec form because distroless has no /bin/sh; replaces the apk-installed /sbin/tini with compose `init: true` or a static tini; drops addgroup/adduser and the `--chown=nextjs:nodejs` names in favour of the nonroot user (uid 65532); keeps the migrate service working with the image's node entrypoint; keeps prod-only api-deps and standalone output; compares size and HIGH/CRITICAL CVE counts with docker image ls and Trivy before switching. Skill-only: #1 (SKILL.md › Facts, native prebuilds; references/dockerfile.md › Distroless or slim), #2 (dockerfile.md › Distroless: healthchecks must use exec form), #4 (dockerfile.md: nonroot uid 65532, not 1001), #6 (dockerfile.md: compare size and CVE count, switch only when the numbers justify it).
assertions: Every stage that runs `npm ci` (deps and api-deps, and the builder if it builds native code) uses a glibc Debian-based Node image (e.g. node:24-bookworm-slim) instead of node:24-alpine, and the answer explains why: the @node-rs/argon2 and @next/swc prebuilds are chosen per libc, so musl node_modules would not load in a glibc distroless runtime
Both HEALTHCHECK instructions (api and web) are rewritten in exec form (a JSON array) because distroless has no /bin/sh; the shell-form `CMD node -e "..."` from the fixture is not kept

The fixture's `ENTRYPOINT ["/sbin/tini", "--"]` (tini installed with apk) is not left pointing at a file that does not exist in distroless: signals and zombie reaping are handled by `init: true` on the app services in compose or by a statically linked tini copied into the image

The runtime stages no longer use `RUN addgroup/adduser` or `COPY --chown=nextjs:nodejs` (those names do not exist in distroless); they run as the image's nonroot user (uid 65532) or a numeric uid, and the answer notes the uid change from 1001

The api and web `CMD` and the migrate service's `command:` are consistent with the runtime image's ENTRYPOINT, so each container ends up running node on dist/server.js, apps/web/server.js or dist/cli/migrate.js (the migrate one from /app/apps/api): distroless nodejs images set the node binary as ENTRYPOINT, so a `CMD`/`command:` that starts with `node` runs `node node ...` unless ENTRYPOINT is reset or replaced (e.g. by a static tini followed by the node path)

Before merging, the answer asks to compare image size and HIGH/CRITICAL CVE counts before and after (e.g. `docker image ls` plus Trivy or Grype on both images) and to keep the switch only if the numbers justify it

evals.prompt: Right now we only find out the Dockerfile is broken when I deploy. Add a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the api and web images on every pull request, fails when an image has serious vulnerabilities, and keeps an SBOM for each image so I can look up later what shipped. We don't push images anywhere yet.
evals.expected_output: A separate workflow (not extra steps in quality.yml) with a matrix over the api and web targets of the one Dockerfile, built with docker/build-push-action and load: true, scanned with Trivy (--exit-code 1 --severity HIGH,CRITICAL), with the SBOM generated from the loaded image (Syft/anchore sbom-action or Trivy SBOM output) and uploaded as an artifact, because BuildKit sbom/provenance attestations are dropped with load: true; read-only permissions, persist-credentials: false, actions pinned by commit SHA and scanner images by digest, no packages: write. Skill-only: #3 (references/ci-supply-chain.md › Build and scan the images: attestations are not stored with load: true), #5 (ci-supply-chain.md › Pinning actions: container images used in workflows pinned by digest).
assertions: Adds a new workflow file (or a new job in a new file) instead of adding the image build to quality.yml, and builds both `--target api` and `--target web` from the single Dockerfile (matrix or two jobs)

A vulnerability scan (Trivy, Grype or equivalent) runs on each built image and fails the job on HIGH/CRITICAL findings that have a fix (only-fixed / --ignore-unfixed); it does not weaken the gate (no lower cutoff, no fail-build: false), and an unfixable or unreachable finding is handled as a reviewed exception with a reason and an expiry date (for Grype, .grype.yaml)

The SBOM is produced in a way that survives a local build: generated from the loaded image (Syft/anchore sbom-action, Trivy `--format cyclonedx|spdx-json`, or similar) and uploaded as a workflow artifact; the answer does not rely on build-push-action `sbom: true`/`provenance` attestations together with `load: true`, or if it mentions them it explains they are dropped by the local image store and need a registry push

Permissions are least privilege: a top-level read-only default (`contents: read`, or `permissions: {}` with per-job `contents: read`), no `packages: write` or other write scope since nothing is pushed, and `actions/checkout` uses `persist-credentials: false`
Every `uses:` is pinned to a 40-character commit SHA, and any scanner or tool container run with `docker run` (e.g. aquasec/trivy) is pinned by `@sha256:` digest rather than a tag such as `latest`

evals.prompt: I'm putting CoinKeeper on the internet at https://budget.example.com on my own server with Docker. The domain's DNS is on Cloudflare with the proxy (orange cloud) turned on. Set up HTTPS and whatever else the app needs to work correctly behind this.
evals.expected_output: A TLS reverse proxy (e.g. Caddy in a compose override or on the host) as the only public entry; web and postgres not reachable from outside; ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://budget.example.com and COOKIE_SECURE true; TRUST_PROXY set to a value the current apps/api/src/config.ts accepts (read from the parser: at the time of writing `true` and hop counts are rejected, IPs/CIDRs/`uniquelocal` accepted) naming only the hop in front of the API; Caddy `trusted_proxies` set to Cloudflare's published ranges (or client_ip_headers CF-Connecting-IP with those ranges) so the client IP is the visitor's, not a Cloudflare edge; a forged X-Forwarded-For check that expects 429 after AUTH_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE attempts; HSTS at the edge. Skill-only: #3 (SKILL.md › Workflow step 4: grep config.ts before choosing a TRUST_PROXY value), #4 (references/compose-runtime.md › Proxy trust: Caddy ignores incoming X-Forwarded-For unless trusted_proxies is set, which is needed only when a CDN sits in front), #5 (compose-runtime.md › Proxy trust: the forged-header rate-limit check).
assertions: Only the TLS proxy is reachable from the internet: the web container's port 3000 and PostgreSQL are not published on a public interface in the production setup (removed with an override such as `ports: !reset []`, or kept bound to 127.0.0.1 with a proxy on the host), and the API stays unpublished
The api gets `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` exactly `https://budget.example.com` and a secure cookie (`COOKIE_SECURE=true`, set explicitly or by stating that the compose default already is true)

`TRUST_PROXY` is set to a value the repository's current `apps/api/src/config.ts` accepts (grader: read the parser; at the time of writing it rejects `true` and hop counts at start-up and accepts IPs, CIDR ranges, `loopback`, `linklocal`, `uniquelocal`), trusting only the hop(s) between the proxy and the API such as the compose network subnet or `uniquelocal`, and the answer shows it read config.ts (or the docs describing its parser) to choose that value

Handles Cloudflare in front of the origin proxy: configures the origin proxy to accept the client address only from Cloudflare's published IP ranges (Caddy `trusted_proxies` with the Cloudflare ranges, optionally `client_ip_headers CF-Connecting-IP`, or the nginx real_ip equivalent) and explains that otherwise every visitor appears as a Cloudflare edge IP and shares sign-in rate-limit buckets; it does not trust forwarded headers from any address (no `0.0.0.0/0` or blanket trust)
Gives a check that the rate limit cannot be dodged with a forged header: more than `AUTH_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE` sign-in requests, each with a different forged `X-Forwarded-For`, must end in `429`
HSTS is set for page responses at the edge (the origin proxy or Cloudflare), since the API's helmet header covers only /api responses

evals.prompt: Make our GitHub Actions more secure and add dependency scanning. The workflows as they are on main are provided at `.claude/skills/container-hardening/evals/files/workflows/quality.yml.txt`, `playwright.yml.txt` and `sonar.yml.txt`, and the Dependabot config at `.claude/skills/container-hardening/evals/files/workflows/dependabot.yml.txt`; treat them as `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `.github/dependabot.yml`.
evals.expected_output: Adds a restrictive top-level permissions block to every workflow (contents: read, or {} with per-job grants), pins every action to a full commit SHA resolved through the peeled tag ref (git ls-remote 'refs/tags/vX^{}' or pinact) with a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` marker despite the repo's no-comments rule (which covers TS/JS only), pins the playwright.yml postgres service image by digest, adds persist-credentials: false where nothing pushes, keeps Dependabot, adds a dependency audit that fails on high severity (npm audit prod-only or full, or OSV-Scanner), CodeQL with security-events: write only on its job, and a CI secret scan over full history (gitleaks with fetch-depth: 0). Skill-only: #3 (references/ci-supply-chain.md › Pinning actions: peeled ref for annotated tags), #4 (ci-supply-chain.md › Pinning actions: images used in workflows by digest), #7 (ci-supply-chain.md › Secret scanning: gitleaks in CI as well as the platform setting).
assertions: Every workflow (the three existing ones and any new one) gets a least-privilege default: a top-level `permissions:` of `contents: read` or `{}` (with per-job `contents: read` where needed); write scopes such as `security-events: write` appear only on the job that uploads CodeQL or SARIF results

Every `uses:` is pinned to a 40-character commit SHA and keeps the version as a trailing marker such as `# v4.2.2` (the repo's no-comments rule applies to TypeScript and JavaScript, not workflow YAML)

The answer says how the SHAs are resolved in a way that yields commit SHAs for annotated tags: the peeled ref (`git ls-remote ... 'refs/tags/vX^{}'`), a tool such as pinact, or an explicit warning that an annotated tag's object SHA is not the commit SHA
The `postgres:17-alpine` service image in playwright.yml is pinned by `@sha256:` digest (tag plus digest), not left on a movable tag
`actions/checkout` gets `persist-credentials: false` in jobs that never push

A dependency audit job fails the build on known high-severity vulnerabilities in package-lock.json: `npm audit --audit-level=high` (production-only with `--omit=dev` or the full tree) or OSV-Scanner on the lockfile

A secret scan runs in CI over the full git history (gitleaks or an equivalent with `fetch-depth: 0`); advising the user to enable GitHub secret scanning and push protection is fine but does not satisfy this on its own

evals.prompt: Some pages feel slow and I want to see which SQL statements take the most time. Can you turn on pg_stat_statements for the Postgres we run in Docker? The compose file as it is on main is provided at `.claude/skills/container-hardening/evals/files/docker-compose.yml.txt`; treat it as the repo's `docker-compose.yml`.
evals.expected_output: Merges `-c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements` into the postgres service's existing `command:` (keeping `log_min_duration_statement=500`), applies it by recreating the postgres container while keeping the named volume, creates the extension once with psql (`CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;`) instead of a Drizzle migration because PGlite, which runs every migration in the Vitest suite, does not provide it, and verifies with SHOW shared_preload_libraries or a query on pg_stat_statements. Skill-only: #1 (references/compose-runtime.md › pg_stat_statements: check for an existing command first), #3 (compose-runtime.md › pg_stat_statements: never in a Drizzle migration, PGlite does not provide it).
assertions: The postgres service's single `command:` preloads the library (`shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements`) and still contains the existing `-c log_min_duration_statement=500`; the existing setting is neither dropped nor split into a second `command:` key

The change is applied without losing data: the postgres container is recreated or restarted in a way that picks up the new command (e.g. `docker compose up -d postgres`) and the `budget-postgres-data` volume is kept (no `down -v`, no new volume)

The extension is created once against the running database with psql (`CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements`), not in a Drizzle migration under apps/api/drizzle, and the answer gives the reason that the Vitest suite runs every migration on PGlite, which does not provide pg_stat_statements
Gives a verification step, such as `SHOW shared_preload_libraries;` or a query on `pg_stat_statements` ordered by total or mean execution time that returns rows
